headline: Majors hold trend structure but momentum fades into resistance; whales moving onto exchanges while retail funding prints extremes in micro-caps.
paragraphs: The regime is split. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and BNB all sit above their 200-day moving averages with golden crosses intact, the textbook frame of an uptrend. XRP, Doge, and ADA have broken below the 200-day line and lack golden crosses, marking them as structurally weaker. The whole market is down 6.63% on the day, which erases much of the month's rally: Bitcoin is up 19.2% on the month but down 5.2% on the week, Ethereum up 29.1% on the month but down 3.3% on the week, Solana up 31.6% on the month yet down 6.2% on the week. Every major asset shows this intra-month reversal pattern. The split between strong holders (BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB) and the rest is real, but the week's losses are real too.

Momentum is neutral to tired across the board. Bitcoin RSI sits at 48.4, Ethereum at 50.4, Solana at 48.4, none of them compressed or extremed, all falling into rest or early fatigue. MACD signals are negative across all seven majors: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Doge, and ADA all print MACD below signal line. The 24-hour moves are red: Bitcoin down 3.2%, Ethereum down 4.6%, Solana down 5.6%, XRP down 10.5%, Doge down 4.4%, ADA down 6.3%. Price is soft, momentum is lagging, and there is no divergence to read as a hidden bid. This is an asset class resting inside a longer uptrend, not being driven upward by conviction.

Derivatives positioning reveals the structural fragility beneath the rally. Bitcoin shows 1.75 longs per short on $2.1 billion open interest with 3.0% annual funding (0.0028% per 8-hour period), a modest long skew being rewarded to stay long. Ethereum at 2.11 longs per short flips into negative funding, meaning shorts are being paid: neg-0.0028% per 8-hour, annual neg-3.0%. Solana worse: 2.29 longs per short yet funding is neg-0.005% per 8-hour (annual neg-5.4%), shorts subsidized to stay short despite 2.3x more longs in the trade. The message is consistent: longer-dated longs are crowded and expensive, shorts are cheap. XRP and Doge break this mold entirely. XRP trades 3.01 longs per short with 11.0% annual funding (0.01% per 8-hour), the tightest, most bullish-positioned micro-cap bet, yet the asset is down 10.5% on the day and sits below its 200-day line. Doge is worse: 4.66 longs per short with 11.0% annual funding, but down 4.4% on the day and structurally broken. These micro-caps are being held by retail on leverage at extremes while the assets deteriorate. Liquidations in the 2-hour window show 100 events on both BTC and ETH with longs hit harder; XRP saw 100 liquidations in 1 hour with longs hit 47 times harder than shorts, and Doge 100 events with longs 140x larger than shorts. The micro-cap funding extremes and violent one-sided liquidation flows suggest thin liquidity and retail crowding.

Whale flows are moving onto exchanges. Over the last 24 hours, net 48.2 million dollars of value flowed onto exchanges, led by Bitcoin: 76.9 million BTC moved onto Binance while only 28.7 million CRO moved off Crypto.com. Zooming back, the week ending September 15 saw 613 million dollars move onto exchanges; the week ending September 8 saw 351 million; August 25 saw 1.09 billion. Whales are liquidating or repositioning into spot liquidity pools on active selling windows. Stablecoin float sits at 310.3 billion, up 1.35% on the month, a rise during a drawdown, meaning holders parked dry powder. ETF flows split: Bitcoin ETF saw an inflow of 159.9 million on the day (14 Sep) but a net outflow of 302.8 million over the last five sessions, a one-day reversal into a weak multi-day trend. Ethereum ETF shows inflow of 121.1 million on the day and 318 million inflow over five sessions, both directions aligned. The traditional-finance bid is tentative and inconsistent on Bitcoin, firm but modest on Ethereum.

Sentiment reads greed at 69 (on a 30-day range of 31 to 74), roughly mid-range for the month, neither extreme. The Fear and Greed gauge is neither a crowded short nor a euphoric long. Against the tape, the split is instructive: retail is crowded into leveraged micro-caps (Doge, XRP) while those assets crack; structural longs (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana) hold their 200-day lines but print no momentum; and whales are stepping into selling windows to move size onto exchanges. The crowd feels greed, but money is not climbing in with conviction; money is rotating, positioning, and taking some chips off in the micro-cap pile where leverage is wildest.

Watch for two conditions: first, whether Bitcoin and Ethereum can hold price above their 200-day SMAs into the close of this session and next, and whether MACD can recross signal line on any major asset to signal re-acceleration. Second, whether whale flows reverse direction (net outflow from exchanges instead of inflow) and whether Ethereum ETF flows persist inbound while Bitcoin ETF remains negative, a potential divergence in traditional-finance demand. The micro-cap liquidation window in XRP and Doge is violent and one-sided; a sudden spike in two-hour liquidation volume or a move further below support would confirm the retail crowding is under acute stress.
